problems: Cliopatria Warring States rows are mislabelled or misplaced, checked cell by cell against the gazetteer: Wei 404..223 lies on the Hebei plain (no Anyi, no Daliang), Han 404..231 sits north of 34.6 N and holds neither Yangzhai nor Xinzheng, Zhao lacks Jinyang and Handan before 366 and holds Shangdang from 404, Yue 500..451 is a subset of Wu. The dossiers replace the geometry with discs at named places (the researcher's reading, rough); 6 Wei shapes are marked wrong, 9 of 10 Han and 15 of 15 Zhao shapes are marked adjust.

Slug collision han: Cliopatria's Han row mixes Warring States Han (han, 404..207) and Liu Bang's Kingdom of Han (new dossier kingdom-of-han, shapes han_-206 and han_-203, predecessor of han-dynasty). Each dossier shows validator warnings 'Cliopatria shape ... has no verdict' for the other's shapes (han 2, kingdom-of-han 7); this is intended, not an omission. The orchestrator should accept the warnings or teach the validator per-name year ranges. The Han row han-2 (Han Cheng, 206-204) continues han; han ends at 207, Cliopatria's handoff.

Shared Wikidata ids are different states: Han Q1968654 with Beylik of Saruhan; Wei Q320930 with Cao Wei; Zhao Q1574107 with Former Zhao (Han-Zhao); Yue Q1936158 with Minyue (a successor of yue, own dossier in another part).
Wikipedia titles: Cliopatria's 'Han (state)' is a disambiguation page (the article is Han_(Warring_States)); Wei_(Warring_States) failed to load (URL_NOT_FOUND), Wei_(state) is the article.
Page budget exceeded for han, wei and zhao (pages shared across the three and the Cliopatria shapes needed checking); 24 distinct pages were opened in all.
wei: two wars (409-406 and 407-406) begin before the state's life (-403..-205) and give validator warnings only; they are the Xihe and Zhongshan campaigns that preceded the partition.

Date disagreements between pages left as noted, not resolved: Qin page 413-409 against Marquess Wen of Wei page 409-406 for Xihe; Zhao annexation of Zhongshan 296 (Zhongshan and Wuling pages) or 295 (Zhao page); Han King An execution 226 (Han page) or 229 (Qin page); Yue end 333 (Yue and Chu pages) against 306 (Spring and Autumn table) against Cliopatria 334.

Revived states kept in one dossier ending at the revival's end: han ends 207 (restored Han, Han Cheng), wei ends 205 (Western Wei, dissolve to kingdom-of-han); lands of the restorations are page-silent (confidence 1).
Zhao ends 222 (end of Prince Jia's Dai regime, Zhao page) against Cliopatria's 226; the 209-205 Zhao line (Zhao Xie) belongs to the ea-02 dossiers dai and chang-shan.
